title: Campaign brief: 'Share Your Real Thing' UGC contest (internal, v3)
content: Proposal before Coca-Cola North America marketing: a six-week user-generated-content contest on TikTok and Instagram Reels under #ShareYourRealThing. Mechanics: consumers post short videos of a real everyday moment with a Coke product; weekly themed prompts; 10 weekly winners ($1,000 each) chosen by a moderation panel; one grand prize (a trip, $25,000 value). Budget: $2.0M total ($600k creator seeding with 40 mid-tier creators, $900k paid amplification, $300k moderation/legal/prizes, $200k agency fees). Targets set by the brief: 100,000 qualifying submissions, 50M organic views, +2pt brand-warmth lift among 16-24s in tracked markets, zero brand-safety incidents severe enough to trigger the crisis protocol. Proposed flight: September 1 - October 12, 2026. The brief notes the launch window requires a go/no-go decision by August 15, 2026 to lock creator contracts.

title: Approval path and constraints (internal)
content: Under Coca-Cola NA's 2026 marketing governance: any consumer-facing campaign over $1M requires (1) a brand-safety review by the risk team (standard turnaround 10 business days from submission of final mechanics; the UGC review checklist covers moderation staffing, takedown SLAs, and contest-law compliance in each state), then (2) sign-off by the NA CMO, Elena Vargas, who has final go/no-go authority; the global office is informed but does not approve NA campaigns at this budget level. Legal must clear contest rules per state before flight start; legal's standard turnaround is 15 business days and can run in parallel with the brand-safety review. The brand-safety review for this brief was submitted on July 24, 2026. As of July 27 neither review has concluded. Vargas has publicly pushed the team toward 'participatory' formats this fiscal year but rejected a prior UGC concept in March 2026 over weak moderation staffing (that brief budgeted 2 moderators; this one budgets 12 with 24/7 coverage).

title: UGC campaign benchmarks relevant to the decision
content: Comparable programs: Coca-Cola's 2014 'Share a Coke' drove roughly +2% US young-adult sales and is the internal gold standard for participatory work. Industry UGC contests on TikTok in 2024-2025 with $1.5-3M budgets and 30-50 seeded creators typically produced 20-80M organic views; submission counts varied wildly (8k to 400k) and correlated most with prompt simplicity and prize cadence. Notable failure mode: unmoderated branded hashtags being hijacked (e.g., McDonald's #McDStories 2012); modern moderation with 24/7 staffing and pre-cleared creator seeds has kept severe incidents rare. Coca-Cola's own 2024 AI-generated holiday ad drew significant public backlash, which the 2025 brand review cited as a reason to favor authentic consumer-made content.
